llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluated tasks, cogito_8b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0638 (median 0) and satisfied just 40 % of the ≥75 % coverage threshold, despite flawless run health (zero infra‑ or endpoint errors). The dominant failure mode was outright omission of tool usage: 248 instances (49.6 % of all tasks) fell into the “no_tool_use” category, followed by task misunderstanding (117 cases, 23.4 %) and early termination (106 cases, 21.2 %). Although the model did make a tool call in roughly half of the attempts (251 calls; 50.2 % of tasks), those cognitive‑only runs (249 tasks) never produced usable evidence, and even when tools were invoked the downstream reasoning was frequently abandoned before any factual claim could be synthesized. To remediate this, we recommend augmenting the prompting framework with a mandatory‑tool‑call check that forces the model to embed at least one verified tool output into its final answer, coupled with a post‑hoc verification step that rejects responses lacking such evidence. What sets cogito_8b_output apart is that its failure profile is driven almost entirely by self‑imposed omission rather than incorrect data handling; the model repeatedly opts not to engage the available MCP APIs, leading to systematic zero‑coverage outcomes despite otherwise stable execution.
